jobs.occupation: Laboratory Technician, QA Lifecycle Laboratory
jobs.description:
Imagine if the quality of both new and existing Coloplast products started with... you.

As our new Laboratory Technician, you will become part of our Quality Assurance Lifecycle Laboratory, where we support products and processes throughout their lifecycle. You will work with ongoing production, helping ensure that our products meet the required quality standards.

If you are motivated by laboratory work, quality assurance, data evaluation, and close collaboration with colleagues across different functions, we offer you an interesting permanent position in a laboratory with a broad range of tasks and stakeholders.

“This is an opportunity to work with quality assurance at different stages of a product’s lifecycle. Your laboratory work and attention to detail will contribute directly to ensuring high-quality products for people with intimate healthcare needs,” says Lotte Stoklund, Team Manager, QA Lifecycle Laboratory.

Join a skilled and collaborative laboratory team

At our Coloplast Mørdrup site, you will join the Quality Assurance Lifecycle Laboratory. The team consists of 10 laboratory technicians and 2 test method specialists who work closely together to support ongoing production, process development, quality investigations, and test method activities.

You will become part of an engaged and supportive team with a strong team spirit and a valuable mix of practical laboratory experience and specialist knowledge. We place great emphasis on engagement, collaboration, and creating a working environment where people feel included, support one another, and share knowledge across tasks and responsibilities. In our daily work, we collaborate closely with colleagues across Quality Assurance, Research and Development, and Operations, and we value curiosity, flexibility, and a continuous improvement mindset.

**Laboratory work across the product lifecycle

**As a Laboratory Technician, you will perform laboratory testing and ensure that results and documentation meet applicable quality requirements. Your tasks will vary depending on production needs, development activities, investigations, and project priorities.

Your primary responsibilities will include:

• 
Planning and performing laboratory tests according to approved procedures, instructions, and test methods

• 
Documenting test activities and results accurately and in accordance with quality requirements

• 
Reviewing and evaluating test results, including basic statistical analysis and interpretation of data

• 
Supporting ongoing production with laboratory testing

• 
Contributing to investigations related to unexpected or non-conforming test results

• 
Supporting test verification and transfer activities

• 
Participating in equipment-related activities, including maintenance, calibration, qualification, and troubleshooting

• 
Writing, reviewing, and updating laboratory procedures, test methods, and work instructions

• 
Supporting change control, corrective and preventive actions, and audit activities

• 
Participating in daily stand-up meetings and contributing to task prioritization and workflow

• 
Ensuring that laboratory activities are carried out in compliance with environmental, health, and safety requirements

• 
Contributing to continuous improvement of laboratory processes, workflows, and ways of working

You can expect a role with both routine and non-routine laboratory activities. You will have the opportunity to build a broad network across the organization and gain experience with quality assurance at several stages of a product’s lifecycle.

**Bring quality and reliability to every laboratory task

**To succeed in this position, you work carefully and systematically and understand the importance of accurate documentation and data integrity. You take responsibility for your tasks, follow established procedures, and

communicate clearly if you identify unexpected results, quality risks or challenges.

You enjoy working both independently and as part of a team. As priorities may change depending on production and project needs, you are flexible and able to organize your work accordingly.

We imagine that you:

• 
Are a qualified Laboratory Technician or have a comparable laboratory education

• 
Have experience with practical laboratory work, preferably within quality control, quality assurance, production, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, or another regulated industry

• 
Have a strong quality mindset and a structured approach to documentation

• 
Have knowledge of basic statistics and experience evaluating and presenting laboratory data

• 
Are able to write and maintain procedures, test methods, and work instructions

• 
Are comfortable working according to procedures, test methods, and quality requirements

• 
Have experience with laboratory equipment and general laboratory practices

• 
Are curious, solution-oriented, and willing to learn new methods and technologies

• 
Work well with colleagues from different professional backgrounds

• 
Communicate clearly and professionally

• 
Are comfortable using digital systems for laboratory documentation and data handling

• 
Are fluent in Danish and able to communicate in English

Experience from the medical device industry, working under Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) requirements, or using a Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) is an advantage, but not a requirement.

**Interested?

**If you would like to know more about the position, please contact Lotte Stoklund, Team Manager, QA Lifecycle Laboratory, at dklst@coloplast.com

We will invite candidates for interviews continuously, so we encourage you to submit your CV with a short description of your motivation for applying as soon as possible. The position will remain open until a suitable candidate is found.

_Pursuing an ambitious growth agenda, Coloplast develops and markets products and services that make life easier for people with intimate healthcare needs. Employing about 16.000 people and with products available in more than 143 countries, we are one of the world´s leading medical device companies. We are constantly growing our business and always looking for new ways to move forward – we explore, learn and look for new ways of doing things.

__Coloplast is committed to being an inclusive organization, where people bring their differences to work each day, fulfil their potential and have a strong sense of belonging because – and not despite – of their differences. jobs.occupation: One or more Professors in Cyber Security
jobs.description:
The Department of Electronic Systems at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for one or more professors in the field of Cyber Security as per March 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The positions are permanent.

**Who we are

**In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems is ranked among the top 50 in the world in the Shanghai Ranking (GRAS). The department employs more than 200 people, of whom approximately 90 are PhD students, and around 40% of all employees are international. In total, the department has more than 800 students enrolled in its BSc and MSc programmes, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and laboratory facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and research results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department here www.es.aau.dk.

The Cyber Security Research Group at Aalborg University (Cyber Security Research Group) is a young and growing research group within the Department of Electronic Systems, focusing on cyber security from various perspectives. Its core research areas are network security, IoT/OT security, applied cryptography, and privacy and security in machine learning. The Cyber Security Research Group consists of 16 members and offers a young, international research environment. The group is responsible for teaching activities in the Master’s programme in Cyber Security, which is taught in English and has more than 100 active Danish and international students. Moreover, the group is strongly engaged in community-building activities, with the AAU Copenhagen campus serving as a hub for weekly CTFs and ethical hacking activities involving dozens of participants.

Your work tasks

You will lead the academic direction of cyber security research and education. The role combines independent academic leadership with close collaboration across the department, within the section, with other research environments, external organisations, and international partners.

Your research and teaching will address one or more areas within applied cryptography, IoT and/or cloud security, security and privacy for big data and machine learning, risk management and threat modelling, mobile security, secure software development, and systems security and privacy. You will initiate and lead research projects, secure and manage external research funding, publish research at an international level, and develop collaborations with industry, public-sector organisations, and universities in Denmark and abroad.

You will teach and supervise students at bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral levels, develop courses and teaching materials, and contribute to the planning and coordination of programmes built on problem-based learning. You will also supervise doctoral researchers and early-career colleagues, contribute to relevant committees and academic activities, and take part in developing the department’s research and educational priorities. International collaboration, including participation in networks, conferences, and joint research activities, forms an integral part of the position.

Your competencies

You hold a doctoral degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, or a closely related field. You have documented original research contributions at an international level within cyber security and a strong publication record in recognised journals and conferences. You can demonstrate a proven track record of attracting, establishing, and managing externally funded research activities, and you have the academic judgement required to develop a coherent research agenda with clear societal and technological relevance.

You bring substantial experience in university teaching, supervision, course development, examination activities, and the development of educational programmes. Familiarity with problem-based learning is relevant, particularly because the role includes contributing to programmes in which students work collaboratively on complex and practice-oriented challenges. You communicate confidently in English, both orally and in writing, and you are willing to develop Danish language skills over time.

You set a clear academic direction while creating constructive working relationships with students, colleagues, and collaborators. You contribute with sound judgement, curiosity, and an ability to turn research ideas into well-organised projects and partnerships. You support the development of early-career researchers, engage openly across disciplines, and help maintain a respectful and collaborative research culture.

**Qualification requirements

**Applicants must be able to document a high degree of original academic production at an international level and experience from teaching at different levels. Including tests/exams, course/study programme management as well as contributions to the development of teaching activities and teaching material.

Emphasis is placed on the extent, to which the applicant, has developed the academic discipline from a research and teaching perspective.

Emphasis may moreover be placed on the applicant’s ability to carry out and develop research-based public-sector consultancy. Also, emphasis will be placed on an assessment of the applicant’s ability to perform research and teaching management tasks and possibly fulfil other functions, for example in relation to the university’s external cooperation.

Emphasis will also be placed on the applicant's ability to undertake pedagogical supervision, supervision and academic assessment work.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma)

• List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment. You may attach a maximum of ten publications.

• Documentation of teaching qualifications. Please see guidelines for teaching portfolio at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design. If this is not enclosed, the applicant must enclose the reasons for this .

• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc.

• Additional qualifications in relation to the position

• References/recommendations

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. The successful applicant is expected, with support from the university, to acquire Danish language skills over time and to be able to contribute to teaching in Danish within 2–5 years of employment, including grading and supervising students, at a level corresponding to the teaching undertaken.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information

Read more about our recruitment process here

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Salary and terms of employment  The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Professor”.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

jobs.occupation: Senior Authorised Person (SAP) – Switching Leader
jobs.description:
Senior Authorised Person (SAP) – Electrical Operations / Switching Leader

Location: Denmark
Employment type: Full-time
Employer: Global Nordics 

Job Description

We are seeking an experienced Senior Authorised Person (SAP) / Switching Leader (Koblingsleder) to support electrical operations on a major engineering project in Denmark.

The successful candidate will be responsible for coordinating safe switching operations, electrical isolations and safety procedures across high-voltage (HV) and low-voltage (LV) electrical systems.

The position operates within an established electrical safety management structure, under the designated Operation Manager (Driftsansvarlig Person), and in accordance with applicable Danish electrical safety regulations and EN 50110-1.

Key Responsibilities

• 
Plan, coordinate and oversee HV and LV switching operations.

• 
Prepare and review switching schedules and electrical safety documentation.

• 
Coordinate electrical isolations, earthing and safe access procedures.

• 
Prepare, issue and cancel safety documents within the scope of assigned authorisation.

• 
Coordinate with Control Engineers and electrical work teams during operational activities.

• 
Ensure appropriate safety precautions are implemented before electrical work begins.

• 
Supervise and coordinate personnel involved in electrical operational activities.

• 
Support commissioning, energisation and electrical system handover.

• 
Maintain accurate switching records, operational logs and safety documentation.

• 
Participate in safety audits, risk assessments and toolbox talks.

• 
Ensure compliance with site-specific electrical safety procedures and applicable Danish regulations.

Qualifications and Experience

• 
Relevant qualification in electrical engineering or equivalent professional experience.

• 
Extensive experience working with HV and LV electrical systems.

• 
Previous experience as a Senior Authorised Person, Switching Leader, Control Engineer or equivalent.

• 
Strong understanding of electrical switching, isolation, earthing and safe working procedures.

• 
Knowledge of EN 50110-1 and electrical safety management systems.

• 
Experience preparing switching schedules and electrical safety documentation.

• 
Demonstrated ability to coordinate electrical work teams and operational activities.

• 
Strong communication, organisational and safety leadership skills.

• 
Good command of English.

Electrical Safety Requirements

The successful candidate will undergo a competence assessment and receive the necessary written operational appointment and authorisation under the project's Danish electrical safety management arrangements (KLS-D) before undertaking regulated electrical activities.

The role does not include statutory Operation Manager responsibilities or electrical installation work requiring separate company authorisation.

Application

Please submit your CV, relevant qualifications and details of your professional experience.

jobs.description:
About Photoncycle

Solar panels make plenty of power in summer and very little in winter, when we need it most. Photoncycle solves that for households. We store energy from the summer sun, so that the it can be used all winter. When there’s excess energy, we sell the surplus to the grid, where it helps balance supply and demand. Households pay a fixed monthly fee; we build, install and operate the system.

Our mission is to accelerate the transition to a more renewable, balanced, and secure energy system. Photoncycle systems enable households to use homegrown energy year-round for electricity, heat, and hot water, while also helping the grid balance production and consumption peaks. This enables the transition away from fossil-based energy.

Our customers are central to that mission. Every home we power is proof that energy independence is possible, and the stories of those homeowners are one of our strongest tools for reaching the next ones.

We are a team of 25 employees across offices in Oslo and Copenhagen. In 2026, we raised a €15 million Series A backed by NordicNinja, Voima Ventures, Lifeline Ventures, Eviny Ventures, Luminar Ventures and Momentum. We're now moving from full-scale pilot to commercial rollout, with the first phase of our production facility coming online in 2027.

The Role

We are looking for a Storyteller to own content creation and community management for our customers. Your main goal is to engage our customers with compelling, on-brand content, and to make Photoncycle something people want to follow, talk about and belong to.

You will shape how Photoncycle shows up on all communications channels, in both Danish and English. That means developing content concepts for social media, writing for our different platforms, and working with external photographers, videographers and agencies to bring ideas to life. You will also be the voice of our brand in our community channels, and you will create moments that bring customers, their neighbours, and future customers together.

Much of this is still unbuilt. Our Danish rollout is in its early phase, so you will spend a considerable amount of time testing formats, trying new ideas, and learning what resonates. We value creativity, curiosity, a structured way of working, and the ability to connect what you create to what the company and the customer actually need, not just the next post in the calendar.

You don't need to be an energy expert from day one. We will support you in learning about the energy markets, and there are experts to help you anytime.

You will join the the small Danish team that is building the market from the ground up, while also contributing to the global storytelling of Photoncycle. You will work closely with operations, product and our marketing colleagues in Oslo to turn a deep-tech product into stories people understand and remember.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop and own the content strategy and content calendar across our channels, in Danish and English, tied to clear goals for engagement, awareness and customer loyalty.

• Shape the Photoncycle brand story, from our mission to the everyday lives of the homeowners who live with our system.

• Develop content concepts and recurring formats for social media that fit how each platform works.

• Write copy for our different platforms, including social media, newsletters, website, customer communication, and customer stories.

• Brief and manage external partners (photographers, videographers, agencies and freelancers) from concept to final delivery.

• Manage our customer community: engage, respond, moderate, spark conversations, and share customer insights with sales, service and product.

• Track performance, report on engagement and reach, and use the data to improve what we do.

What We're Looking For

Must-have experience

• Experience with concept development, content strategy and creation, brand storytelling or social media, in-house or at an agency.

• Excellent written Danish and strong written English.

• A solid understanding of the logic of social media platforms: algorithms, formats, and what drives reach and engagement.

• Strong project management skills: able to run several projects in parallel and deliver on time.

• Ability to explain complex or technical topics in plain, human language.

• Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where the right answer isn't known yet.

Nice-to-have

• Experience working with external partners to produce content, such as video and images.

• Experience with community management or building online and offline communities.

• Background in energy, climate tech, home improvement, or other considered consumer purchases.

• Hands-on skills in short-form video, photo editing or design tools, for example CapCut, Adobe or Canva.

• Experience with social analytics, newsletter tools, CRM, or paid social.

We welcome applicants across experience levels, from motivated early-career storytellers to more senior profiles. If you bring a strong creative sense and genuine curiosity for this domain, we encourage you to apply even if you do not match every item above exactly.

What Success Looks Like

• Photoncycle has a recognisable, consistent brand voice that customers and prospects engage with.

• Our customers feel part of a community and share their experience with neighbours, friends and online.

• Content formats, partners and processes are in place so we can produce high-quality content at a steady pace, and scale it to new markets.

• The team makes better marketing and customer decisions by bringing engagement data and customer insight into the discussion, and you'll be part of making that happen.

What We Offer

• The opportunity to shape the voice of a high-impact climate technology company in one of its first markets.

• A central role in connecting Photoncycle's customers, product and brand.

• A collaborative, mission-driven culture with significant ownership.

• An office in the heart of Copenhagen at BLOXhub with lunch benefits and unlimited coffee.

Photoncycle is committed to building an inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and make hiring decisions based on skills, experience, and potential.

Are you passionate about using atomistic simulations and machine learning to accelerate the green transition? Do you want to understand, atom by atom, why electrolysers degrade, and design materials that make them last longer? Do you have a background in computational chemistry, physics, materials science or chemical engineering?

Then this PhD opportunity at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) might be the perfect fit for you. We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student for the project ATOMIZE: Atomistic Stabilization in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells, a collaboration between DTU Physics and Topsoe, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF).

Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells (SOEC) are among the most efficient technologies for producing green hydrogen, but their long-term stability remains a key challenge for large-scale deployment. In this PhD project, you will use density functional theory and state-of-the-art machine-learning interatomic potentials to study SOEC electrode materials at the atomic scale and at length scales that were previously out of reach. The aim is to understand what governs electrode stability and how it can be improved. You will validate your simulations against advanced experimental characterization data.

In practice, you will be hired at DTU Physics and join the Computational Catalysis group led by Associate Professor Alexander Bagger. The group has a long-term goal to develop predictive models and schemes for new reactions and materials in close connection with experiments. The project aims to discover catalytic materials capable of converting CO₂ directly into carbon nanotubes (CNTs), combining climate-change mitigation with the sustainable production of next-generation functional materials. 

Carbon nanotubes are among the most sought-after nanomaterials due to their exceptional strength, low weight, electrical conductivity, and thermal stability. They are key components in future energy technologies, electronics, and lightweight structural materials. Yet, conventional CNT production relies on fossil-derived feedstocks and carries a substantial carbon footprint. This PhD project seeks to establish an entirely new catalytic paradigm in which captured CO₂ becomes the raw material for producing high-value carbon nanomaterials. 

You will join the Catalysis and Operando Characterization (CATOC) group at DTU, an international research environment at the forefront of catalyst development and operando characterization. jobs.description:
Department of Plant and Environmental Science, Faculty of Science at University of Copenhagen is offering a 34-months Postdoc position in Crop root development, and its effects on root zone water and nitrogen dynamics commencing February 1st 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  Further information on the Department is linked at https://plen.ku.dk/english/.  Inquiries about the position can be made to Professor Kristian Thorup-Kristensen, email: ktk@plen.ku.dk.

  Job description
 The postdoc will be working on crop root and root zone research in our newly established root research facility RootAccess (https://plen.ku.dk/english/research/crop_sciences/cpps/rootaccess/). The facility is equipped to allow the study of crop root growth to 3 meters depth and to follow the dynamic effects on soil water and nitrogen (uptake, leaching and denitrification) to the same depth. During the project, a number of common crops will be grown in rotation in the facility, allowing the study of their different exploitation of the root zone for water and nitrogen, both during the crop growth seasons as well as during periods without crops, to cover rotational effects over the years. Studies will be based on soil water sensors, minirhizotrons, soil water suction cells, and soil gas samplers, all installed at several depths in the soil profile. Furthermore, we use isotopic tracers to follow root uptake. The postdoc will be part of the team working on the project and facility, and co-responsible for running the experiments in the facility. Apart from the experimental work and contribution to publishing the results, a main task for the postdoc will be to produce well organized datasets and clear result presentation, continuously updated during the project.

  Description of the scientific environment
 The postdoc will be hosted in the Crop Physiology and Production Systems research group (https://plen.ku.dk/english/research/crop_sciences/cpps/), which focuses on crop growth and quality at the crop, crop rotation, and cropping system level. The group has a specific focus on crop root research, using field-scale root research facilities, including the RadiMax root phenotyping facility as well as the newly developed RootAccess facility.

  Required qualifications
 The applicants should hold professional and personal skills and qualifications as stated below:

   	
• A PhD degree in agricultural science, or related disciplines. 	
• Solid knowledge of whole plant and crop physiology, including plant and soil water and nutrient relations. 	
• Good technical skills and practical experimental experience with whole plant or preferably field crop experiments, as well as modern plant analyses and monitoring techniques. 	
• Competent on data management and statistical analysis, etc. 	
• Good record, considering your early career stage, of peer-reviewed scientific publications 	
• Good interpersonal skills, experience with collaborative work in multinational teams. 	
• Excellent English writing and speaking abilities.   Key criteria for the assessment of candidates

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the position 	
• Scientific publications 	
• Relevant research experience 	
• Other professional activities 	
• Language skills   Terms of employment
 The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector at www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish)

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include 

   	
• Motivation letter 	
• Curriculum vitae 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of 3 particularly relevant papers   The deadline for applications is 15 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. Interviews are expected to be held in week 50 2026.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.
